Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is developing a screenless fitness band similar to WHOOP or Fitbit Air. After using WHOOP for six months, I genuinely believe this direction is correct, but there are several areas I hope Apple can do better.

Since the product is still in early development stages, we don't yet know the specific design of Apple's screenless fitness band, and it may not launch until 2028. Bloomberg described it as "a slim fabric band with built-in sensors and computing modules."

Earlier this year, WHOOP partnered with Chase to offer discounts or free WHOOP devices to Sapphire credit card holders—I was one of the beneficiaries. I started using WHOOP around that time, but I never managed to use it consistently with full commitment.

The reason is simple: automatic workout detection is never 100% accurate, and I find it troublesome to deliberately pull out my phone to log workouts—whether before or after exercise. Apple Watch can start tracking directly from the watch face, while WHOOP can sync timing through Apple Health. This is also the main reason I keep wearing my Apple Watch.

If I'm working out at the gym, pulling out my phone is still acceptable, but if I'm just casually cycling or taking a walk, I don't want to bother taking out my phone to log the activity.

So for Apple's screenless fitness band, I sincerely hope they can add a combination of buttons and indicator lights, so users can start and stop workout tracking. Categorising the activity type would still require a phone afterwards, but I'd rather deal with that after the workout than fiddle with it during exercise. Apple could also develop classification models based on various factors.

Summary

If Apple succeeds in making a screenless fitness band that's easy to use and doesn't rely on a phone, I think it would be quite appealing. This design has several advantages, including more comfortable wear, longer battery life, and the ability to wear a traditional watch at the same time.

Personally, after evaluating WHOOP, I actually still lean towards wearing a smartwatch, even at the expense of battery life. I understand some people want a screenless design to avoid distractions, but for me, simply turning on the watch's "Do Not Disturb" mode solves that problem.

What are your thoughts on Apple developing a screenless fitness band? How much would you be willing to pay for it? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
